questions.question: You change a normal C# field on one game instance, but the value on another instance stays the same. Why?
answers: The instances are running at different frame rates
Each instance has its own copy of the field
The NetworkObjectId changes when the field changes
The server waits for the owner to copy the field

questions.question: What does a NetworkObject primarily add to a GameObject?
answers: A NetworkVariable for each serialized field
Transform synchronization
A network identity for the spawned object
Client authority for the object's owner

questions.question: A client is the owner of a NetworkObject. Which statement is correct?
answers: Ownership identifies the owning client; it doesn't automatically grant authority
Ownership makes NetworkVariables owner-writable
Ownership makes transforms owner-authoritative
Ownership gives the client spawn control

questions.question: A client tries to pick up a shared item. What should normally happen?
answers: The client takes ownership and changes the item
The client requests the pickup, and the server validates and applies it
The client changes the item first, and the server relays the result
The client sends the result directly to the other clients

questions.question: A door is opened during the game. Players joining later should see that it is already open. How should its open/closed state normally be synchronized?
answers: A NetworkVariable storing the current state
An RPC sent whenever the door opens
A local bool on each client
An ownership change when the door is used

questions.question: The server confirms a projectile hit. Current clients should be notified when it happens, but players joining later should not receive the old event. What best fits this job?
answers: A NetworkVariable storing that a hit occurred
An RPC sent when the hit is confirmed
A local variable on the shooter
A NetworkObject ownership change
